layers.note: Turns spring prairies and oak savannas blue; a staple food plant of the Coast Salish peoples.

moisture.note: Ground wet in spring and dry by summer; prairie swales.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,500 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

coldest_c.note: Maritime and inland winters both: coldest-month means from about −10 °C (gone by −16 °C), as from the coast to the interior mountains.

hard_freeze_c.note: Cold-hardy: lows to about −34 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −42 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 14 to 25 °C; gone below 11 °C, where summers are too short, and above 29 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,800 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,100.

degree_days_5.note: About 800 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 400: from the lowlands to the montane forest.

moisture_index.note: Across its range, a moisture index from about 0.32, gone by 0.2.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit; its range takes in summer-dry coasts and interior mountains with some summer rain, to about 0.45 of the year's precipitation.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Common camas grows in moist spring meadows from British Columbia to California and east to Montana and Wyoming (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
